courses.title: Advanced Machine Learning and AI
courses.description: Core principles of machine learning and deep learning. Theoretical foundations of optimization, probabilistic modeling, and representation learning. Modern strategies include contrastive, positive-unlabeled, and reinforcement learning with applications across domains.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, CS major, and C or better in CS 3310 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.description: Architecture and organization of high performance computers. Principles of instruction sets. Pipelining, instruction level parallelism and multiprocessor. Memory, storage, and interconnection. Quantitative analysis and evaluation of design alternatives. Historical developments. Architectural tradeoffs and innovations.

courses.title: Advanced Algorithm Design and Analysis
courses.description: Advanced problem domains, including graph problems, pattern matching, compression, network flow and transforms. Amortized and average case analysis. Lower bounds. Approximation techniques. Probabilistic algorithms.

courses.title: Advanced Software Engineering
courses.description: Software metrics and models. Software development methodologies. Advanced topics in object-oriented software engineering. Formal methods for modeling and specification. Software architecture. Software testing. Survey of trending software engineering tools and researches.

courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Topics chosen according to the interests and needs of the students.

courses.title: Advanced Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Advanced study of natural language processing focusing on deep and state-of-the-art methods. Topics include full lexical, syntactic, and semantic analysis; neural models such as RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and transformers; contextual embeddings (e.g., BERT, GPT); retrieval-augmented and multilingual NLP applications. Emphasis on theoretical foundations, implementation of advanced models, and engagement with current research literature.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3310 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Information Retrieval
courses.description: Theory, design, and implementation of text-based information retrieval systems. Overview of information retrieval system. Statistical characteristics of text, representation of information needs and documents, retrieval models, search evaluation, clustering and classification algorithms. Current issues and technologies in information retrieval development.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CS 4190 Core principles of computer vision, focusing on image formation, representation, and feature extraction as the basis for visual understanding. Theoretical foundations include camera models, geometric reasoning, illumination, and feature learning. Modern approaches extend these principles with convolutional networks and transformer-based models for recognition, detection, and interpretation across diverse domains.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3310 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Software for Intelligent Robotics
courses.description: Dual Listed as: CS 4240 Design and development of software systems for intelligent robotics. Emphasis on software architectures, algorithms, and frameworks that enable robotic autonomy. Topics include robot control paradigms and behavior design, perception and sensing pipelines, and software approaches for navigation, planning, localization, and mapping.

courses.title: Distributed Intelligence in Robotics
courses.description: Multi-robot architecture, multi-robot taxonomies, multi-robot communication, and the state-of-the-art research issues in this field, such as swarm intelligence, multi-vehicle collaboration, task allocation, multi-robot or human-robot teaming, and reconfigurable robotics.
courses.prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 3310 ; and CS 256 or CS 2560 .

courses.title: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles
courses.description: Examines Connected Vehicle (CV) and Autonomous Vehicle (AV) technologies, including vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V), vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I), and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication systems. Topics include intelligent transportation systems, mobility as a service, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), sensor fusion, localization, planning, and cybersecurity issues specific to connected and autonomous vehicles. Emphasis on hands-on projects and case studies to reinforce theoretical concepts.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CS 3310 or related course; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Computability and Complexity Theory
courses.description: Formalizing problems and algorithms. Characterizations and properties of complexity classes, undecidability. Cook-Levin Theorem, NP-complete problems, proof of NP-completeness.
courses.prerequisites: CS 311 or CS 3110 ; and CS 331 or CS 3310 .

courses.title: Parallel and Distributed Algorithms
courses.description: Models of parallel and distributed computation. Design and analysis of algorithms for parallel and distributed systems. Basic techniques, classic problems. Parallel and distributed complexity classes. Hardware and software issues involved in parallel and distributed problem solving.

courses.title: Scheduling Algorithms
courses.description: The alpha/beta/gamma notation. Scheduling theory. Deterministic scheduling. Basic scheduling algorithms. Single machine models. Parallel machine models. Other scheduling models. Real-time scheduling. Applications.

courses.title: Topics in Compiler Design
courses.description: Code generation and optimization. Data flow analysis. Syntax-directed translation. Parallelizing compiler. Automatic compiler generation.

courses.title: Advanced Information Security
courses.description: Information security overview. Information security attacks and defenses case studies in systems, networking, web application and cloud computing.

courses.title: Digital Image Processing
courses.description: Mathematical preliminaries for digital image processing. Digital image fundamentals sampling and quantization. Image enhancement spatial and frequency domain filtering. Image compression. Color image processing. Multiresolution processing.
courses.prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 3310 ; and C or better in MAT 214 or MAT 2250 .

courses.title: Data Privacy and Security
courses.description: Privacy Policies. Challenges of sensitive data leakage. Definitions of data privacy. Privacy enhancing techniques: cryptographic approaches and non-crypto approaches. Metadata privacy. Anonymous communication systems. Machine learning and privacy. Block-chain and data integrity. Big data privacy.

courses.title: Machine Learning for Cyber Security
courses.description: The fundamentals of Machine Learning algorithms, building Machine learning information security models, Malware detection system, spam email detection system, botnet detection system, network security, security application for deep learning, and anomaly detection system.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CS 3310 , or consent of instructor. Knowlegability in Python preferred.

courses.title: Game Theory and its Applications in Communication Networks
courses.description: Fundamentals in game theory, strategic games, extensive games, coalitional games, Nash equilibrium and other solution concepts. Packet forwarding games, medium access games for 802.11 WLAN, power control games in CDMA systems.
courses.prerequisites: CS 3800 or CS 380, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Networks
courses.description: Issues in network architectures and standards. Network design. Performance evaluation and monitoring. Network management and security. High-speed networking technologies. Wireless networks and mobile computing. System architecture and network programming.

courses.title: Distributed Computing Systems
courses.description: Distributed systems models. Distributed naming. Synchronization. Consistency. Fault tolerance. Security. Grid computing. Computational Cloud. Distributed storage systems. Peer-to-Peer systems. Software defined Networks.

courses.title: Computational Social Systems
courses.description: In-depth exploration of computational techniques for representing, modeling, processing, and analyzing social information. Topics include complex adaptive systems theory, modeling and simulation techniques, and the use of parallel and distributed processing tools to manage large-scale and dynamic social data. Examine challenging problems in modeling social interactions, focusing on security and privacy concerns in the context of data analysis. Applications and case studies will illustrate real-world implications across areas such as social networks, public policy, and digital media, providing practical insights into the complexities of social systems.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CS 3310 or related course; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Human Computer Interaction
courses.description: Principles of human factors, computer technology, and their interactions. Theory and practice of user interface design and evaluation. Special topics such as graphical user interface, graphics programming, multisensory systems, and computer-supported cooperative work

courses.title: Topics in Database Systems
courses.description: Advanced SQL programming. Trigger and stored procedure. Object-relational and semi-structured modeling and databases. Physical database design. Techniques and algorithms for database design. XML and Web data. Distributed databases. Information integration. Data warehouses. Data mining. Current research topics and technologies in database systems.

courses.title: Software Verification and Validation
courses.description: Techniques for evaluating software quality and integrity. Quality assessment, proof of correctness, testing methods and tools. Survey of trending researches in software testing and verification.

courses.title: Software Metrics and Models
courses.description: Measuring internal product attributes (size and structure). Program decomposition (control-flow graph, prime components, sequencing and nesting). Hierarchical measures. Test coverage measures. Basis coverage du-path coverage. Complexity measures. Modularity and information flow measures. Coupling and Cohesion measures. Object-oriented metrics. Software cost estimation models. Software reliability models. Measuring external product attributes (modeling and measuring software quality).

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.

courses.title: Advanced Data Mining
courses.description: Advanced methods for extracting patterns in large data sets that blend traditional data analysis with machine learning algorithms. Strong emphasis on data preprocessing and post-processing techniques, including sampling, feature selection, dimensionality reduction, statistical testing, and data visualization. Topics include classification, regression, clustering, association rule mining, and anomaly detection, with a focus on scalability, model evaluation, and interpretable, theoretically grounded approaches.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, CS major, and C or better in CS 3310 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project
courses.description: Independent work on practical application of an existing methodology or procedure under supervision of a project advisor. Credit assigned upon successful completion of project and oral presentation. Total credit limited to 1 unit, but may be repeated until completion. May be taken unlimited times for a total credit of 1 unit. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: CS 691 or CS 6940 , GWT*, Advancement to Candidacy, and approval of project committee.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 1 unit, but may be repeated until completion.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Independent investigation intended to be an extension of an existing body of knowledge. Reporting of research results in an oral presentation and acceptable written form. Credit assigned upon successful completion of thesis and oral presentation. May be taken unlimited times for a total credit of 3 units. *The enforcement of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement has been temporarily suspended per a Chancellor’s Office memorandum.
courses.prerequisites: CS 691 or CS 6940 , GWT*, Advancement to Candidacy, and approval of thesis committee.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units, but may be repeated until completion.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
